jess: heads-up — canary for raven-lite-2.2-int4 shows funcall/JSON-parse spike during streaming. parse failures up from ~0.8% to 9.4% on tool calls that return a numeric id field.

arjun: uhoh. any pattern in the failures?

jess: yes — frequent patterns: trailing comma at end of object, sometimes `id: null` instead of number, and occasionally the model emits an extra `\n` inside the JSON chunk boundary. sample from a failed call below: 

```
{"action":"create_ticket","args":{"id":, "title":"User issue",}}
```

or 

```
{"action":"create_ticket","args":{"id": null, "title":"timeout repro"}}
```

jess: our schema validator rejects both. the interesting bit — these only show up in int4 canary, int8 baseline is fine.

claire: could be quantization-induced tokenization boundary noise for numeric tokens (digits), or the model's tendency to hallucinate `null` when low-confidence numeric tokens collapse.

arjun: can we reproduce offline deterministically? run a small replay of the canary payloads with `--seed=42` and collect tokenstream diffs. also add streaming chunk boundaries to logs.

jess: ran a 2k sample replay. diffs show an extra `,` token in 6% of failing traces right before `}` — looks like a tokenization split: e.g., `"id" : "12"` -> streamed as `"id" : "1` + `2"` then post-processing recombines wrong.

arjun: ok. immediate mitigations:
- bump parse retry budget from 1 -> 3 for canary route (cheap)
- apply a tolerant preprocessor that attempts quick repairs: strip trailing commas, coerce `"id": null` -> remove-field or attempt numeric parse.
- tag telemetry with `funcall_parse_mode` = `relaxed-int4-canary` so we can separate impact.

claire: are we comfortable with auto-coercing `null` -> number? might mask real errors. I prefer removing the field when null and letting downstream handle absence.

jess: agreed — implement removal for null numeric fields. also add a small heuristic: if schema expects integer and value is a quoted number string, coerce to int.

deploy-bot: canary deploy complete: raven-lite-2.2-int4 -> slot canary-3 (10% traffic) at 2026-03-19T16:12:15Z

eva: quick note — this'll affect evals. our structured-output evals (schema compliance) should snapshot pre/post, run exact-match + relaxed-match metrics. add a new column for "postprocessor repairs" so we don't conflate model quality with repair heuristics.

arjun: good call. i'll add `repaired=true/false` tag to telemetry and instrument the eval harness to compute: raw_schema_failure_rate, repaired_success_rate, and final_acceptance_rate.

jess: after implementing fixes locally:
- parse failures drop from 9.4% -> 2.1% on sampled canary replay\- repaired_success_rate ~ 75% of previous failures

claire: still not ideal — 2.1% is non-trivial for primetime. next steps?

arjun: medium-term: try int4 quantization with higher-fidelity numeric tokenization (adjust tokenizer merges or use hybrid int8 for numeric-heavy heads). also ramp up KV-prefix anchoring to reduce split tokens across chunks.

jess: will open two follow-up PRs: one for the preprocessor + retry budget (hotfix), one for quantization/tokenizer adjustments (experiment track).

jess: PR notes drafted: include sample failing traces, before/after numbers, and the telemetry tag list. tagging @claire @arjun for review. :eyes:

claire: ack. add a short canary-run checklist: e.g., run 5k sampled eval, verify repaired vs raw deltas, check latency impact of preprocessor (<2ms target).

arjun: i'll own the replay harness changes and the telemetry keys. jess — ping when hotfix PR is up so we can canary again.

jess: on it. thanks all. :thumbsup:
